text.p: These are the main headlines on Hungary's Kossuth Radio midday news. Reuters cannot vouch for their accuracy:
- Opposition parties said in the parliament that amendments on the penal code were not severe enough.
- Budapest continues the reconstruction of the Circle, the main road of the city centre.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs, visiting Japan, confirmed in Tokyo that the NATO would not station nuclear weapons nor permanent troops in Hungary even after the country joins the organisation.
- Croatian President Franjo Tudjman said in Budapest that ethnic Croats in Hungary would be allowed to receive Croatian citizenship.
- The government does not support Cuba's claim for organising a World Youth Festival.
